subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a good and a service?
options: A service can be stored but a good cannot
A good cannot be sold for profit
A good is a physical, tangible product while a service is an intangible activity provided for a customer
A good is always cheaper than a service
questions.explain: Goods are tangible physical products, whereas services are intangible activities performed for customers.

questions.q: On a break-even chart, the break-even point is shown where:
options: The revenue line reaches its highest point
The total revenue line crosses the total costs line
questions.explain: Break-even occurs where the total revenue line crosses the total costs line, so revenue exactly covers costs.

questions.q: For taking on risk, an entrepreneur's main potential reward is:
options: Profit and being their own boss
questions.explain: In return for risk, entrepreneurs can earn profit and gain independence, though success is not guaranteed.

questions.q: The margin of safety is:
options: The total amount of fixed costs
The difference between actual sales and the break-even level of sales
questions.explain: Margin of safety is how far actual (or planned) sales exceed the break-even output.

questions.q: Which is a common reason why new businesses fail?
questions.explain: Running out of cash (poor cash-flow management) is one of the most common causes of business failure.

questions.q: A business in the public sector is one that is:
options: Always run to make maximum profit
Owned and run by the government
questions.explain: The public sector is owned and controlled by the government, usually to provide public services.

questions.q: Sampling in market research is used because:
options: Asking a representative group is quicker and cheaper than surveying the whole population
It avoids the need for any data
It is impossible to ask anyone at all
questions.explain: A sample lets a business gather views from a representative group rather than surveying everyone, saving time and money.

questions.q: A business charges a high price to suggest premium quality and exclusivity. This pricing strategy is called:
questions.explain: Premium pricing sets a deliberately high price to signal a high-quality, exclusive product.

questions.q: Which of the following lists the 4 Ps of the marketing mix?
questions.explain: The marketing mix is made up of Product, Price, Place and Promotion.

questions.q: Which of these is a long-term source of external finance?
options: A mortgage repaid over many years
questions.explain: A mortgage is repaid over many years, making it a long-term external source of finance.

questions.q: What is the main role of an entrepreneur when starting a business?
options: To work only as an employee for a larger firm
To guarantee the business will make a profit
To take a risk by organising resources to set up a business
questions.explain: An entrepreneur takes the risk of combining resources (land, labour, capital) to create a new business.

questions.q: What does 'limited liability' mean for the owners of a private limited company (Ltd)?
options: The business has limited time to operate
Owners can lose only the amount they invested
Owners are personally responsible for all business debts
questions.explain: Limited liability means shareholders can only lose the money they invested, not their personal assets.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of e-commerce for a business?
options: It always removes the need for marketing
It allows the business to sell to customers 24 hours a day across a wide area
It limits sales to local customers only
questions.explain: E-commerce lets a business sell online around the clock to a much larger geographic market.

questions.q: Which of the following are the three factors of production?
questions.explain: The factors of production are land, labour and capital (with enterprise often added as a fourth).

questions.q: A business has revenue of 200,000 pounds and gross profit of 80,000 pounds. Its gross profit margin is:
questions.explain: Gross profit margin = (gross profit / revenue) x 100 = (80,000 / 200,000) x 100 = 40%.

questions.q: How is profit calculated?
questions.explain: Profit = total revenue - total costs.

questions.q: In a partnership, profits are usually:
questions.explain: Partners typically share the profits (and losses) of the business according to their agreement.

questions.q: What is enterprise in a business context?
options: The skill of spotting an opportunity and taking the risk to act on it
questions.explain: Enterprise involves identifying a business opportunity and taking the risk of acting on it.

questions.q: During which stage of the product life cycle do sales rise quickly?
questions.explain: In the growth stage, sales increase rapidly as the product becomes more popular.

questions.q: A cash-flow forecast is used to:
options: Predict future cash coming in and going out
questions.explain: A cash-flow forecast predicts the timing of cash inflows and outflows to spot shortages early.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a sales promotion?
options: A 'buy one get one free' offer
questions.explain: Sales promotions are short-term incentives such as BOGOF offers, discounts or free gifts to boost sales.

questions.q: Product differentiation means:
options: Selling the same product as every competitor
Making a product stand out from rivals through features, design or branding
questions.explain: Differentiation makes a product distinct from competitors' offerings, helping to attract and keep customers.
